boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Reams' Station (August 25) record (August 25, 1864) in the Richmond-Petersburg Campaign [June 1864-March 1865]. Globe Tavern (VA072) ends on August 21; the June 29 Reams' Station record (VA068) is separate. Army-wide returns, raid-wide and multi-action loss totals, and the siege as a whole are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 3,492 total and the live field 3,556 (US 2,742; CS 814). Humphreys gives Hancock's loss as 610 killed and wounded and 1,762 missing (2,372) with nine guns lost, and Hill's report of 720 lost and 12 colors, 9 guns, 2,150 prisoners and 3,100 small arms taken; Lee's dispatch gives seven colors, 2,000 prisoners and 9 guns.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Hill's and Lee's prisoner and colors counts differ.

open_questions: Hancock's, Miles's, Gibbon's and Gregg's reports (Volume XLII Nos. 17, 19, 47, 229), Hill's and Hampton's reports (Nos. 372, 374) and the compiled returns remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC (the live NPS page and the frozen Arnold rows) is one family. Humphreys' The Virginia Campaign of ’64 and ’65 (1883) is an interested history by the Army of the Potomac's chief of staff, later commander of its Second Corps, in the same author family as the registered From Gettysburg to the Rapidan; it relies on Meade's, Hancock's, Warren's, Burnside's, Parke's and Wilson's reports and quotes Lee's, Beauregard's and Gordon's despatches, so it is not independent of those families. Gillmore's, Meade's, Hancock's, Burnside's, Wilson's, Hampton's, Stannard's and Lee's papers, printed in Official Records Series I, Volumes XXXVI (Part 2), XL, XLII and XLVI (Part 1), are separate families of interested commanders' accounts; each volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Lee's telegrams largely relay subordinates' reports. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
